lead: Digital World Acquisition / DWAC — Truth Social launches on a closed market
smaller: Bitcoin / BTC-USD — digital gold flunks the weekend war test
ARK Innovation ETF / ARKK — Cathie Wood keeps the dip-buying faith
Gold Miners ETF / GDX — the old haven still earns its keep
why_lead: Truth Social's App Store release was a dated pending catalyst for Monday 21 February (Reuters n0932, Axios n1766), landing on a US market holiday, with saturation-level mainstream coverage as the attention evidence (Newsweek n1723, Vanity Fair n1744, Snopes rumour check n1755, Reuters testers n1742, Forbes n1722). DWAC closed at 84.32 USD on 18 February, +15.32% over 20 sessions and +2.83% over five against a falling Nasdaq 100 (-1.14%) and Robinhood (-11.34% 5s), a simple repeatable buy-the-rumour story. Nunes's end-of-March full-operation timetable (n1765) and the same-week Virgin Galactic round trip (n0523, n0903, SPCE 5s -0.47%) supply the break and the analog. No strictly earlier retail notes or drafts existed when this date was written, so there is no prior lead to repeat; the launch outcome itself is after the cutoff and is not used.
why_smaller: Bitcoin: the weekend's only open market fell 4.21% on 20 February and 13.78% over five sessions, Ether -17.33%, a week after the Super Bowl crypto ad blitz (Bloomberg n0360, Seattle Times n0086) and as Buterin welcomed another winter (n1001); distinct narrative of digital gold failing the war test while gold rose 3.13% 5s, with US-listed proxies (MARA, COIN) yet to price the weekend slide.

ARKK: buy-the-dip faith in the innovation complex, driven by Cathie Wood's 'way undervalued' and misallocation-of-capital headlines (CNBC n1741, Business Insider n1757) against ARKK -4.96% on 18 February and -9.87% 5s, Roblox -25.58% 5s, Bloomberg's year-from-peak piece (n1720) and a 2Y yield up 46 bps over 20 observations.

GDX: the old-fashioned safe-haven war trade, gold 1,899.80 USD/oz (+3.13% 5s) and GDX +6.38% 5s as Biden said he was convinced Putin had decided to invade (BBC n1424), nuclear drills (n1422) and extended Belarus drills (n1435); breaks on the Macron summit track (n1430) or rate pressure (n1776).
considered_not_chosen: DraftKings (DKNG -21.62% on 18 February, -25.89% 5s): largest 1-session drop on the card, but no own-date headline on its results beyond a generic sports-betting-margins piece (n1119), so no supportable catalyst or attention evidence.
Upstart (UPST +30.02% 5s, -6.86% 1s): big post-results swing but only a generic 'is now a good time to scoop up' piece (n0576).
Virgin Galactic / SPAC King exit (SPCE -6.77% 1s; n0843, n0844, n0903, n0523): used as the lead's same-week analog rather than a separate item to keep four distinct narratives.
Roblox and Shopify post-earnings crashes (n0117, n0631, n0640): folded into the ARKK dip-faith item.
Defense stocks (ITA -0.84% 5s, LMT -2.46% 5s): no war-trade rally on the card yet, so no lead case.

Avoided as possibly after the cutoff or misdated: n1427 and n1440 (Biden agreeing in principle to meet Putin, a White House statement that may post-date 00:00 UTC 21 February), n1319 (CNN 'Photos: Russia invades Ukraine', stamped 14 February, misdated), Reuters LIVE MARKETS blogs (n1274, n1264, n1229, n1218).
